description: I’m a student innovator interested in AI, software, electronics, space technology, and real-world problem solving. I enjoy turning ideas into working prototypes and combining different technologies. I have experience with AI projects, web development, Arduino/ESP32, hardware prototyping, INSPIRE-MANAK, and Teen Tycoons at BITS Pilani. I’m looking for teammates interested in space, data, programming, research
summary: AstraNova gives every astronaut a digital twin: an AI copy of their body that learns their own normal, from Earth baseline to space baseline, and warns about health problems up to 48 hours ahead. It watches heart rate, blood pressure, sleep, hydration and cabin air, checks each change against cited NASA research, and explains it in plain words with a checklist a non-doctor crew member can follow. Urgent alerts reach the crew and the Crew Medical Officer first, then flight surgeons on Earth. This matters because no doctor is on board, and messages to Mars take 4 to 24 minutes one way. On simulated missions, the model warned before 12 of 12 problems, with a median warning of about 44 hours. It is a research prototype, not a diagnosis tool, and all results so far come from simulated data.
details:
AstraNova runs as a Python backend (FastAPI) with a browser screen. Each astronaut's readings are compared to their own personal normal for each activity and mission phase. A fast check looks at today; a slow check looks for drift over several days. Cabin CO2 and water data are linked to the crew's breathing and hydration, so if the whole crew's breathing rises together, the system suspects the cabin air before illness.

The prediction model is a Random Forest (scikit-learn) on 17 body, cabin and check-in signals, predicting a problem in the next 48 hours across five problem types. It is tested by leave-one-astronaut-out validation, so no astronaut's data is used in both training and testing. Every decision shows seven visible steps and its research source. If the backend stops, the device falls back to baseline statistics and then fixed rules.

Tools: Python, FastAPI, scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy, joblib, JavaScript, HTML. Optional: Google Gemini and xAI Grok to reword answers, and Gemini Live for voice. A number check rejects any answer with a figure not in the facts.

Creative points: the digital twin per astronaut, the cabin-air link, and the escalation chain (crew, Crew Medical Officer, flight surgeons). Our team considered privacy, the honesty of simulated data, and keeping alerts calm so people don't ignore them.

Impact: earlier warning on long missions where no doctor is on board.
